# greymemory

> A self-hosted memory engine for AI agents. It extracts atomic memories from conversations, detects contradictions, supersedes stale facts while keeping their full history, and serves the current truth through hybrid BM25 + vector search — all on SQLite, with any LLM and embedder you bring. No cloud dependency, no API lock-in, no data leaving your server. Scores 80.0% on LongMemEval, versus a funded cloud startup's 83.4%.

This site is a live, interactive knowledge-graph console rendered over a real [LongMemEval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813) ingestion (the full benchmark run is 25,000+ extracted memories across 86 users; the hosted demo serves four of those users, live from SQLite). The landing page walks the whole argument: the five memory abilities as worked conversation examples, ChatGPT (57.7%) vs Coze (33.0%) scored on the same questions, a reader-noise table (oracle context vs full history per model), an animated ingestion pipeline that resolves a real contradiction, the three edge types, a time-travel timeline you can scrub, and a retrieval walkthrough. At the bottom sits the real graph: hover a node to read the memory, click one to light its neighborhood (seed → EXTENDS expansion → supersession chain), and press the one-click "try" question to run a real `memory.search()` against the live database and watch retrieval light up the graph. Built for the Razorpay AI Builders challenge — proof of work over a résumé.

Contradictions are resolved at write time: an LLM classifier detects UPDATES / EXTENDS relationships, supersedes stale facts, and keeps full version history for time-travel queries, profiles, and derivations. Three memory types (fact · preference · episode); three edge types (UPDATES · EXTENDS · DERIVES). ESM · Node 18+ · better-sqlite3 · provider-agnostic by design.

## The problem it solves

Long-term memory for AI is unsolved. On LongMemEval, GPT-4o scores 91.8% reading a chat history offline, but ChatGPT's own long-term memory scores 57.7% on the same questions and Coze scores 33.0%. Even handed the whole transcript in its context window, GPT-4o loses a third of its accuracy to surrounding noise: 87.0% → 60.6% (the "lost in the middle" effect — bigger context windows make it worse, not better). Having the information isn't using it.

The paper distills what a memory must do into five abilities, all of which greymemory targets:

- Information Extraction — recall one specific detail from months of conversation.
- Multi-Session Reasoning — synthesize an answer scattered across many sessions.
- Knowledge Updates — notice a fact changed and answer with the current one, not both.
- Temporal Reasoning — reason about when things happened, not just what.
- Abstention — know what it doesn't know, and say so instead of confabulating.

## Approach — the paper's indexing → retrieval → reading design

greymemory implements the LongMemEval paper's recommended optimization at all four control points, and adds hybrid retrieval the paper's design lacks:

- CP1 · Value — round-level chunk granularity (indexing).
- CP2 · Key — fact-augmented chunk embeddings, K = V + fact (+9.4% recall).
- CP3 · Query — LLM-extracted time-aware query expansion (+6.8–11.3% recall on temporal questions).
- CP4 · Reading — Chain-of-Note + structured JSON answering (up to +10 points accuracy).

## Benchmark results (LongMemEval, official LLM-as-judge)

| Category | context window (GPT-4o) | greymemory | Supermemory (cloud) |
|---|---|---|---|
| single-session-user | 81.4% | 93.3% | 97.1% |
| single-session-assistant | 94.6% | 93.3% | 96.4% |
| knowledge-update | 78.2% | 80.0% | 88.5% |
| temporal-reasoning | 45.1% | 73.3% | 76.7% |
| single-session-preference | 20.0% | 66.7% | 70.0% |
| multi-session | 44.3% | 66.7% | 71.4% |
| overall | 60.6% | 80.0% | 83.4% |

96% of a funded cloud startup's accuracy — self-hosted, from SQLite, at $0.013 per session of ingestion. On the categories where a memory engine actually matters (preference, temporal, multi-session) greymemory delivers +47, +28, +22 points of lift over just dumping the history into the context window.

## Install

`npm install greymemory` — published on npm (ESM, Node 18+, better-sqlite3 under the hood). Bring your own LLM and embedder as two async functions; `npx greymemory init` scaffolds the config.

## Links

- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/greymemory): `npm install greymemory` — the library itself.
- [Live interactive console](https://greymemory-arun-dev-des-projects.vercel.app/): the force-directed knowledge-graph demo over a real LongMemEval ingestion.
- [Live graph API](https://greymemory-console-production.up.railway.app/api/viz/datasets): the JSON backend behind the demo — `/api/viz/datasets`, `/api/viz/graph?dataset=greymemory&container=<id>`, `/api/viz/question/<container>`; live search is rate-limited per IP.
- [Source code (GitHub)](https://github.com/arun-dev-des/greymemory): the full memory engine, benchmark runner, and this console.
- [LongMemEval paper (arXiv 2410.10813)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813): the benchmark and the indexing → retrieval → reading framework greymemory implements.
